paragraphs.text: 1.Personal pronoun
A pronoun replace a noun in Tagalog sentence to make the sentence less repetitive. Two important types of tagalog pronoun that are often used
personal pronouns ( ako,kami,tayo,ikaw,kayo,siya and sila ) and
demonstrative pronouns ( ito,iyan and iyon ).
The ff. Pronouns are nominative in form and can only be used as the subject of a verb
in a sentence.

The pronoun ako is the equivalent of the English pronoun / and, when used as a subject, can come at the beginning of the sentence before the verb or, in the inverted word order, after the predicate, as in the following examples:
Ako ay si John. I am John.
Ako ay lalaki . I am a man.
Masipag ako . I am industrious.
Malusog ako . I am healthy.

AKO is linked by AY to the predicate in the first two sentences above using the subject-predicate word order. Note chat in this type of sentence, ay may be shortened to 'y when the preceding word ends in a vowel . The shortened form 'y is also used after kami (we including he/she, and), tayo (we including you, he/she, and /), and other pronouns ending in vowels.
Ako'y si John.		I am John.
Ako'y lalaki .		I am a man.
Ako'y nag- aaral .		I am studying. Kami’y nag aaral We are studying

slides.title: 2 .THE PERSONAL PRONOUNS KAMI AND TAYO (MEANING WE)

paragraphs.text: The pronoun we is expressed by KAMI and TAYO in Tagalog.
Kam i means we in the sense of he/she and I excluding the person spoken to , whereas Tayo means we in the sense of you, he/she, and I, or you (the person spoken to) and I.
Kami ay sina John at Lisa. We are John and Lisa.
Kami'y magkapatid . We are brothers and sisters.
Masipag Industrious/Hardworking
Magkaibigan Friends
Magkapatid Siblings
Mahirap Poor; difficult
Marami			Plenty Maniwala Believe
Mababait kami We are good.
Mahirap kami. We are poor.
It is important to remember that pronouns may come at the beginning of the sentence before the verb or at the end of the sentence after the predicate depending on the word order.
Tayo ay sina John at Mary.		We are John and Mary.
Tayo'y magkaibigan .		We are friends.
Mababait tayo.			We are good.
Masisipag tayo.			We are industrious.

slides.title: 3. The personal pronouns IKAW and KAYO (meaning you)

paragraphs.text: The pronoun IKAW is used to express YOU when it is used at the beginning of the sentence , however in the inverted word order where the subject comes after the predicate, it is shortened to ka.
lkaw ay si Mary.		You are Mary.		Si Mary ka.
lkaw ay babae .		You are a woman.	Babae ka.
Masipag ka.		You are industrious.	Ikaw ay masipag .
Malusog ka.		You are healthy		Ikaw malusog .
KAYO is the plural form of IKAW excluding the speaker . Kayo ay sina John at Lisa		You are John and Lisa Kayo ay magkakapatid .		You are brother and sister (siblings)
Malulusog kayo			You are heathy

slides.title: 4 . The personal pronouns siya and sila (meaning he/she and they )

paragraphs.text: The pronoun SIYA is singular meaning he or she .
Siya ay si Peter.		He is Peter.
Siya’y isang bata.		He is a child.
Marunong siya .		He is intelligent.
Mabait siya .		She is good.
The plural form of SIYA is SILA meaning they .
Sila ay sina John at Mary. They are John and Mary.
Sila ay magkaibigan . They are friends.
Marurunong sila . They are intelligent .
In a polite or formal situation, either one of the plural pronouns kayo and sila may replace the singular pronoun ikaw or ka in sentences and questions to indicate respect.
Kayo po ba ay guro ? 			 Are you a teacher, sir/madam?
Sila po ba ay guro ? 			 Are you a teacher, sir/madam?
Kayo ay mabait .				You (plural) are kind.
